source_refs.note: Exercise 3.2 Q2 (i)-(xiii), by change of variable; answers printed in the key block 'Exercise 3.4'

blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{e^{x}}{9-e^{2x}}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
\(e^{2x} = (e^{x})^{2}\) and \(e^{x}dx\) is the differential of \(e^{x}\).
With \(u = e^{x}\) the integral is \(\int\frac{du}{3^{2}-u^{2}}\), special integral (i) of Section 3.3 with \(a = 3\).
Plan: substitute, use the formula, put \(x\) back.
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{e^{x}}{9-e^{2x}}\,dx\)
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: change of variable \(u = e^{x}\), then the special integral \(\int\frac{du}{a^{2}-u^{2}} = \frac{1}{2a}\ln\left|\frac{a+u}{a-u}\right| + c\).

Change of variable
\[u = e^{x},\quad du = e^{x}\,dx\]
\[e^{2x} = (e^{x})^{2} = u^{2}\]
Why: the numerator \(e^{x}dx\) becomes \(du\) exactly.

Use the special integral with \(a = 3\)
\[\int\dfrac{du}{3^{2}-u^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2(3)}\ln\left|\dfrac{3+u}{3-u}\right| + c\]
Why: \(9 = 3^{2}\), so the denominator has the form \(a^{2} - u^{2}\).

Put \(x\) back
\[= \dfrac{1}{6}\ln\left|\dfrac{3+e^{x}}{3-e^{x}}\right| + c\]
Why: \(u = e^{x}\).

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[\tfrac{1}{6}\big(\ln|3+e^{x}| - \ln|3-e^{x}|\big)\Big]\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{6}\Big(\dfrac{e^{x}}{3+e^{x}} + \dfrac{e^{x}}{3-e^{x}}\Big)\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{6}\cdot\dfrac{6e^{x}}{9-e^{2x}} = \dfrac{e^{x}}{9-e^{2x}}\]
Why: the integrand comes back.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text:
The answer key prints this question's answers under the heading 'Exercise 3.4' (the block headed 'Exercise 3.2' holds the answers of Exercise 3.5).
Q2 (i)-(viii) are 1 (i)-(viii); Q2 (x), (xi), (xii) keep their numbers; Q2 (ix) is printed as (xiv) and Q2 (xiii) as (xv).
The key's (ix) \(2 - \frac{\pi}{2}\) and (xiii) \(\frac{\pi}{8}\ln 2\) are definite-integral values that belong to no question of this exercise.

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{\cos x}{\sin^{2}x-4}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
\(\cos x\,dx\) is the differential of \(\sin x\).
With \(u = \sin x\): \(\int\frac{du}{u^{2}-2^{2}}\), the Challenge formula (i) with \(a = 2\).
Plan: substitute, formula, put \(x\) back.
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{\cos x}{\sin^{2}x-4}\,dx\)
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: \(u = \sin x\), then \(\int\frac{du}{u^{2}-a^{2}} = \frac{1}{2a}\ln\left|\frac{u-a}{u+a}\right| + c\).

Change of variable
\[u = \sin x,\quad du = \cos x\,dx\]
Why: the numerator becomes \(du\).

Use the formula with \(a = 2\)
\[\int\dfrac{du}{u^{2}-2^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2(2)}\ln\left|\dfrac{u-2}{u+2}\right| + c\]
Why: the denominator has the form \(u^{2} - a^{2}\).

Put \(x\) back
\[= \dfrac{1}{4}\ln\left|\dfrac{\sin x-2}{\sin x+2}\right| + c\]
Why: \(u = \sin x\). Since \(-1 \le \sin x \le 1\), this also equals \(\frac{1}{4}\ln\frac{2-\sin x}{2+\sin x} + c\).

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[\tfrac{1}{4}\big(\ln|\sin x-2| - \ln|\sin x+2|\big)\Big]\]
\[= \dfrac{\cos x}{4}\Big(\dfrac{1}{\sin x-2} - \dfrac{1}{\sin x+2}\Big)\]
\[= \dfrac{\cos x}{4}\cdot\dfrac{4}{\sin^{2}x-4} = \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin^{2}x-4}\]
Why: the integrand comes back.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iii) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{e^{x}}{1+e^{2x}}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Again \(e^{2x} = (e^{x})^{2}\) and \(e^{x}dx = d(e^{x})\).
With \(u = e^{x}\): \(\int\frac{du}{1+u^{2}} = \tan^{-1}u + c\).
Plan: substitute and use the \(\tan^{-1}\) formula with \(a = 1\).
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{e^{x}}{1+e^{2x}}\,dx\)
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: \(u = e^{x}\), then \(\int\frac{du}{a^{2}+u^{2}} = \frac{1}{a}\tan^{-1}\frac{u}{a} + c\) with \(a = 1\).

Change of variable
\[u = e^{x},\quad du = e^{x}\,dx\]
\[\int\dfrac{e^{x}\,dx}{1+(e^{x})^{2}} = \int\dfrac{du}{1+u^{2}}\]
Why: the numerator becomes \(du\) and \(e^{2x} = u^{2}\).

Integrate and put \(x\) back
\[= \tan^{-1}u + c = \tan^{-1}(e^{x}) + c\]
Why: \(\frac{d}{du}\tan^{-1}u = \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\).

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\tan^{-1}(e^{x}) = \dfrac{e^{x}}{1+e^{2x}}\]
Why: chain rule gives the integrand.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iv) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{1}{x\sqrt{4-(\ln x)^{2}}}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
\(\frac{1}{x}dx\) is the differential of \(\ln x\).
With \(u = \ln x\): \(\int\frac{du}{\sqrt{2^{2}-u^{2}}}\), special integral (ii) of Section 3.3 with \(a = 2\).
Plan: substitute, use \(\sin^{-1}\), put \(x\) back.
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{dx}{x\sqrt{4-(\ln x)^{2}}}\)
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: \(u = \ln x\), then \(\int\frac{du}{\sqrt{a^{2}-u^{2}}} = \sin^{-1}\frac{u}{a} + c\).

Change of variable
\[u = \ln x,\quad du = \dfrac{1}{x}\,dx\]
\[\int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{4-(\ln x)^{2}}}\cdot\dfrac{dx}{x} = \int\dfrac{du}{\sqrt{2^{2}-u^{2}}}\]
Why: \(\frac{d}{dx}\ln x = \frac{1}{x}\).

Integrate and put \(x\) back
\[= \sin^{-1}\dfrac{u}{2} + c = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\ln x}{2}\right) + c\]
Why: special integral (ii) with \(a = 2\).

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{\ln x}{2} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-\frac{(\ln x)^{2}}{4}}}\cdot\dfrac{1}{2x}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{4-(\ln x)^{2}}}\]
Why: \(\sqrt{1 - \frac{p}{4}} = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{4-p}\), and the 2s cancel.

blocks.prompt: 2 (v) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{1}{9x^{2}-25}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
\(9x^{2} - 25 = (3x)^{2} - 5^{2}\), a difference of squares.
With \(u = 3x\) (so \(dx = \frac{du}{3}\)) it is \(\frac{1}{3}\int\frac{du}{u^{2}-5^{2}}\).
Plan: substitute, use the \(u^{2} - a^{2}\) formula with \(a = 5\).
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{dx}{9x^{2}-25}\)
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: \(u = 3x\), then \(\int\frac{du}{u^{2}-a^{2}} = \frac{1}{2a}\ln\left|\frac{u-a}{u+a}\right| + c\).

Change of variable
\[u = 3x,\quad du = 3\,dx,\quad dx = \dfrac{du}{3}\]
\[\int\dfrac{dx}{(3x)^{2}-5^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{3}\int\dfrac{du}{u^{2}-5^{2}}\]
Why: \(9x^{2} = (3x)^{2}\) and \(25 = 5^{2}\).

Use the formula with \(a = 5\)
\[= \dfrac{1}{3}\cdot\dfrac{1}{2(5)}\ln\left|\dfrac{u-5}{u+5}\right| + c\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{30}\ln\left|\dfrac{u-5}{u+5}\right| + c\]
Why: \(\frac{1}{3}\cdot\frac{1}{10} = \frac{1}{30}\).

Put \(x\) back
\[= \dfrac{1}{30}\ln\left|\dfrac{3x-5}{3x+5}\right| + c\]
Why: \(u = 3x\).

Check
\[\dfrac{1}{30}\Big(\dfrac{3}{3x-5} - \dfrac{3}{3x+5}\Big)\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{30}\cdot\dfrac{30}{9x^{2}-25}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{9x^{2}-25}\]
Why: the derivative of the answer is the integrand.

blocks.prompt: 2 (vi) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{dx}{x\sqrt{3x^{2}-12}}\)
blocks.explanation:
Take 3 out of the root: \(\sqrt{3x^{2}-12} = \sqrt{3}\sqrt{x^{2}-4}\).
\(\sqrt{x^{2}-2^{2}}\) is Case 3: put \(x = 2\sec\theta\) (take \(x > 2\)).
Plan: substitute, simplify to \(\int d\theta\), go back to \(x\).
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{dx}{x\sqrt{3x^{2}-12}}\), \(x > 2\)
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: trigonometric substitution, Case 3 (\(\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}\), \(x = a\sec\theta\)), because \(\sec^{2}\theta - 1 = \tan^{2}\theta\) removes the root.

Take the common factor out of the root
\[\sqrt{3x^{2}-12} = \sqrt{3(x^{2}-4)} = \sqrt{3}\sqrt{x^{2}-4}\]
\[I = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\int\dfrac{dx}{x\sqrt{x^{2}-4}}\]
Why: the root now has the Case 3 form with \(a = 2\).

Substitute \(x = 2\sec\theta\), \(0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}\)
\[dx = 2\sec\theta\tan\theta\,d\theta\]
\[\sqrt{x^{2}-4} = \sqrt{4\sec^{2}\theta - 4}\]
\[= 2\sqrt{\tan^{2}\theta} = 2\tan\theta\]
Why: \(\sec^{2}\theta - 1 = \tan^{2}\theta\), and \(\tan\theta > 0\) on this interval.

Simplify and integrate
\[I = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\int\dfrac{2\sec\theta\tan\theta\,d\theta}{(2\sec\theta)(2\tan\theta)}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\int\dfrac{1}{2}\,d\theta = \dfrac{\theta}{2\sqrt{3}} + c\]
Why: everything cancels except \(\frac{1}{2}\).

Back to \(x\)
\[\sec\theta = \dfrac{x}{2} \Rightarrow \theta = \sec^{-1}\dfrac{x}{2}\]
\[I = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}\sec^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) + c\]
Why: from the substitution \(x = 2\sec\theta\).

The answer key's form
\[\tan\theta = \sqrt{\sec^{2}\theta-1} = \dfrac{\sqrt{x^{2}-4}}{2}\]
\[\theta = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{\sqrt{x^{2}-4}}{2}\]
Why: so the key's \(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}\arctan\left(\frac{\sqrt{x^{2}-4}}{2}\right) + c\) is the same answer for \(x > 2\).

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}\sec^{-1}\tfrac{x}{2}\Big]\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}\cdot\dfrac{2}{x\sqrt{x^{2}-4}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}\,x\sqrt{x^{2}-4}} = \dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{3x^{2}-12}}\]
Why: \(\frac{d}{dx}\sec^{-1}\frac{x}{a} = \frac{a}{x\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}}\) for \(x > a\).

blocks.prompt: 2 (vii) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{x^{2}}{x^{2}+a^{2}}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
\(x^{2} + a^{2}\) suggests Case 2: \(x = a\tan\theta\) (take \(a > 0\)).
Then \(x^{2} + a^{2} = a^{2}\sec^{2}\theta\) and the integral becomes \(a\int\tan^{2}\theta\,d\theta\).
Plan: substitute, use \(\tan^{2}\theta = \sec^{2}\theta - 1\), go back to \(x\).
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{x^{2}}{x^{2}+a^{2}}\,dx\), \(a > 0\)
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: Case 2 substitution \(x = a\tan\theta\), because \(\tan^{2}\theta + 1 = \sec^{2}\theta\).

Substitute \(x = a\tan\theta\), \(-\frac{\pi}{2} < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}\)
\[dx = a\sec^{2}\theta\,d\theta\]
\[x^{2}+a^{2} = a^{2}\tan^{2}\theta + a^{2} = a^{2}\sec^{2}\theta\]
Why: \(\frac{d}{d\theta}\tan\theta = \sec^{2}\theta\); the identity simplifies the denominator.

Simplify
\[\int\dfrac{a^{2}\tan^{2}\theta}{a^{2}\sec^{2}\theta}\cdot a\sec^{2}\theta\,d\theta\]
\[= a\int\tan^{2}\theta\,d\theta\]
Why: \(a^{2}\) and \(\sec^{2}\theta\) cancel.

Integrate
\[= a\int(\sec^{2}\theta - 1)\,d\theta\]
\[= a(\tan\theta - \theta) + c\]
Why: \(\tan^{2}\theta = \sec^{2}\theta - 1\) and \(\int\sec^{2}\theta\,d\theta = \tan\theta\).

Back to \(x\)
\[a\tan\theta = x,\quad \theta = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{x}{a}\]
\[= x - a\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right) + c\]
Why: from \(x = a\tan\theta\).

A quicker way
\[\dfrac{x^{2}}{x^{2}+a^{2}} = 1 - \dfrac{a^{2}}{x^{2}+a^{2}}\]
\[\int = x - a^{2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{a}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x}{a} + c\]
Why: dividing first, then the \(\tan^{-1}\) formula, gives the same answer.

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[x - a\tan^{-1}\tfrac{x}{a}\Big] = 1 - \dfrac{a^{2}}{x^{2}+a^{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{x^{2}}{x^{2}+a^{2}}\]
Why: the integrand comes back.

blocks.prompt: 2 (viii) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{1}{x\left[1+(\ln x)^{2}\right]}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
\(\frac{dx}{x}\) and \(\ln x\) together: \(u = \ln x\).
Then the integral is \(\int\frac{du}{1+u^{2}} = \tan^{-1}u + c\).
Plan: substitute, \(\tan^{-1}\), put \(x\) back.
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{dx}{x[1+(\ln x)^{2}]}\)
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: \(u = \ln x\), then the \(\tan^{-1}\) formula with \(a = 1\).

Change of variable
\[u = \ln x,\quad du = \dfrac{dx}{x}\]
\[\int\dfrac{1}{1+(\ln x)^{2}}\cdot\dfrac{dx}{x} = \int\dfrac{du}{1+u^{2}}\]
Why: \(\frac{d}{dx}\ln x = \frac{1}{x}\).

Integrate and put \(x\) back
\[= \tan^{-1}u + c = \tan^{-1}(\ln x) + c\]
Why: \(\int\frac{du}{1+u^{2}} = \tan^{-1}u + c\).

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\tan^{-1}(\ln x) = \dfrac{1}{1+(\ln x)^{2}}\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}\]
Why: this is the integrand.

blocks.prompt: 2 (ix) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{1}{x^{2}\sqrt{x^{2}+4}}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
\(\sqrt{x^{2}+2^{2}}\) is Case 2: \(x = 2\tan\theta\).
The integral becomes \(\frac{1}{4}\int\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin^{2}\theta}d\theta\), a simple substitution in \(\sin\theta\).
Plan: substitute, integrate, return to \(x\) with a right triangle.
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{dx}{x^{2}\sqrt{x^{2}+4}}\)
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: Case 2, \(x = 2\tan\theta\), because \(1 + \tan^{2}\theta = \sec^{2}\theta\) removes the root.

Substitute \(x = 2\tan\theta\), \(-\frac{\pi}{2} < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}\)
\[dx = 2\sec^{2}\theta\,d\theta\]
\[\sqrt{x^{2}+4} = \sqrt{4\tan^{2}\theta+4} = 2\sec\theta\]
Why: \(\sec\theta > 0\) on this interval.

Simplify
\[I = \int\dfrac{2\sec^{2}\theta\,d\theta}{(4\tan^{2}\theta)(2\sec\theta)}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{4}\int\dfrac{\sec\theta}{\tan^{2}\theta}\,d\theta\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{4}\int\dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin^{2}\theta}\,d\theta\]
Why: \(\frac{\sec\theta}{\tan^{2}\theta} = \frac{1}{\cos\theta}\cdot\frac{\cos^{2}\theta}{\sin^{2}\theta}\).

Integrate (put \(v = \sin\theta\), \(dv = \cos\theta\,d\theta\))
\[\dfrac{1}{4}\int v^{-2}\,dv = -\dfrac{1}{4v} + c\]
\[= -\dfrac{1}{4\sin\theta} + c\]
Why: power rule with \(n = -2\).

Back to \(x\)
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{x}{2} \Rightarrow \sin\theta = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x^{2}+4}}\]
\[I = -\dfrac{\sqrt{x^{2}+4}}{4x} + c\]
Why: in a right triangle with opposite side \(x\) and adjacent side 2 the hypotenuse is \(\sqrt{x^{2}+4}\).

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big(-\dfrac{\sqrt{x^{2}+4}}{4x}\Big)\]
\[= -\dfrac{1}{4}\cdot\dfrac{\frac{x^{2}}{\sqrt{x^{2}+4}} - \sqrt{x^{2}+4}}{x^{2}}\]
\[= -\dfrac{1}{4}\cdot\dfrac{x^{2} - (x^{2}+4)}{x^{2}\sqrt{x^{2}+4}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{x^{2}\sqrt{x^{2}+4}}\]
Why: quotient rule gives the integrand.

blocks.prompt: 2 (x) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{dx}{(1+x^{2})^{3/2}}\)
blocks.explanation:
\((1+x^{2})^{3/2} = (\sqrt{1+x^{2}})^{3}\): Case 2 with \(a = 1\), \(x = \tan\theta\).
Then \((1+x^{2})^{3/2} = \sec^{3}\theta\) and the integral is \(\int\cos\theta\,d\theta\).
Plan: substitute, integrate, return to \(x\) with a triangle.
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{dx}{(1+x^{2})^{3/2}}\)
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: Case 2, \(x = \tan\theta\).

Substitute \(x = \tan\theta\), \(-\frac{\pi}{2} < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}\)
\[dx = \sec^{2}\theta\,d\theta\]
\[1 + x^{2} = \sec^{2}\theta\]
\[(1+x^{2})^{3/2} = \sec^{3}\theta\]
Why: \((\sec^{2}\theta)^{3/2} = \sec^{3}\theta\) since \(\sec\theta > 0\) here.

Integrate
\[\int\dfrac{\sec^{2}\theta}{\sec^{3}\theta}\,d\theta = \int\cos\theta\,d\theta\]
\[= \sin\theta + c\]
Why: \(\frac{1}{\sec\theta} = \cos\theta\).

Back to \(x\)
\[\tan\theta = x \Rightarrow \sin\theta = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^{2}}}\]
\[= \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^{2}}} + c\]
Why: right triangle with opposite \(x\), adjacent 1, hypotenuse \(\sqrt{1+x^{2}}\).

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^{2}}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{1+x^{2}} - \frac{x^{2}}{\sqrt{1+x^{2}}}}{1+x^{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{(1+x^{2})^{3/2}}\]
Why: quotient rule gives the integrand.

blocks.prompt: 2 (xi) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{dx}{x\sqrt{x^{2}-9}}\)
blocks.explanation:
\(\sqrt{x^{2}-3^{2}}\) is Case 3: \(x = 3\sec\theta\) (take \(x > 3\)).
Everything cancels to \(\frac{1}{3}\int d\theta\).
Plan: substitute, integrate, return to \(x\).
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{dx}{x\sqrt{x^{2}-9}}\), \(x > 3\)
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: Case 3, \(x = 3\sec\theta\), because \(\sec^{2}\theta - 1 = \tan^{2}\theta\).

Substitute \(x = 3\sec\theta\), \(0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}\)
\[dx = 3\sec\theta\tan\theta\,d\theta\]
\[\sqrt{x^{2}-9} = \sqrt{9\sec^{2}\theta - 9} = 3\tan\theta\]
Why: \(\tan\theta > 0\) on this interval.

Simplify and integrate
\[\int\dfrac{3\sec\theta\tan\theta\,d\theta}{(3\sec\theta)(3\tan\theta)} = \dfrac{1}{3}\int d\theta\]
\[= \dfrac{\theta}{3} + c\]
Why: \(\sec\theta\tan\theta\) cancels.

Back to \(x\)
\[\sec\theta = \dfrac{x}{3} \Rightarrow \theta = \sec^{-1}\dfrac{x}{3}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{3}\sec^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) + c\]
Why: this agrees with Challenge formula (v) with \(a = 3\).

The answer key's form
\[\tan\theta = \sqrt{\sec^{2}\theta - 1} = \dfrac{\sqrt{x^{2}-9}}{3}\]
\[\dfrac{\theta}{3} = \dfrac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{\sqrt{x^{2}-9}}{3}\]
Why: the key's \(\frac{1}{3}\arctan\left(\frac{\sqrt{x^{2}-9}}{3}\right) + c\) is the same for \(x > 3\). (For \(x < -3\) use \(\frac{1}{3}\sec^{-1}\left|\frac{x}{3}\right| + c\), as in Example 28.)

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[\tfrac{1}{3}\sec^{-1}\tfrac{x}{3}\Big] = \dfrac{1}{3}\cdot\dfrac{3}{x\sqrt{x^{2}-9}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{x^{2}-9}}\]
Why: the integrand comes back.

blocks.prompt: 2 (xii) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \sqrt{\frac{1+x}{1-x}}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Defined for \(-1 \le x < 1\). Multiply inside the root by \(\frac{1+x}{1+x}\) to get \(\frac{1+x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\).
\(\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\) is Case 1: \(x = \sin\theta\).
Plan: rationalise, substitute, integrate \(1 + \sin\theta\), return to \(x\).
steps:
Given: \(\int \sqrt{\frac{1+x}{1-x}}\,dx\), \(-1 \le x < 1\)
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: make the denominator \(\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\), then Case 1, \(x = \sin\theta\).

Rationalise
\[\sqrt{\dfrac{1+x}{1-x}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{(1+x)^{2}}{(1-x)(1+x)}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1+x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\]
Why: \(\sqrt{(1+x)^{2}} = 1 + x\) because \(1 + x \ge 0\).

Substitute \(x = \sin\theta\), \(-\frac{\pi}{2} \le \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}\)
\[dx = \cos\theta\,d\theta,\quad \sqrt{1-x^{2}} = \cos\theta\]
\[\int\dfrac{1+\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\cdot\cos\theta\,d\theta = \int(1+\sin\theta)\,d\theta\]
Why: \(1 - \sin^{2}\theta = \cos^{2}\theta\) and \(\cos\theta \ge 0\) here.

Integrate
\[= \theta - \cos\theta + c\]
Why: \(\int\sin\theta\,d\theta = -\cos\theta\).

Back to \(x\)
\[\theta = \sin^{-1}x,\quad \cos\theta = \sqrt{1-x^{2}}\]
\[= \sin^{-1}x - \sqrt{1-x^{2}} + c\]
Why: from \(x = \sin\theta\).

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[\sin^{-1}x - \sqrt{1-x^{2}}\Big]\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}} + \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1+x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1+x}{1-x}}\]
Why: the integrand comes back.

blocks.prompt: 2 (xiii) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}{x}\,dx\ (a > 0)\)
blocks.explanation:
\(\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}\) is Case 1: \(x = a\sin\theta\).
The integral becomes \(a\int\frac{\cos^{2}\theta}{\sin\theta}d\theta = a\int(\csc\theta - \sin\theta)d\theta\).
Plan: substitute, split, integrate, return to \(x\).
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}{x}\,dx\), \(a > 0\)
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: Case 1, \(x = a\sin\theta\), because \(1 - \sin^{2}\theta = \cos^{2}\theta\).

Substitute \(x = a\sin\theta\), \(-\frac{\pi}{2} \le \theta \le \frac{\pi}{2}\), \(\theta \ne 0\)
\[dx = a\cos\theta\,d\theta\]
\[\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}} = a\cos\theta\]
Why: \(\cos\theta \ge 0\) on this interval.

Simplify
\[I = \int\dfrac{a\cos\theta}{a\sin\theta}\cdot a\cos\theta\,d\theta\]
\[= a\int\dfrac{\cos^{2}\theta}{\sin\theta}\,d\theta = a\int\dfrac{1-\sin^{2}\theta}{\sin\theta}\,d\theta\]
\[= a\int(\csc\theta - \sin\theta)\,d\theta\]
Why: split the fraction into two terms.

Integrate
\[= a\ln|\csc\theta - \cot\theta| + a\cos\theta + c\]
Why: \(\int\csc\theta\,d\theta = \ln|\csc\theta - \cot\theta|\) and \(\int\sin\theta\,d\theta = -\cos\theta\).

Back to \(x\)
\[\csc\theta = \dfrac{a}{x},\quad \cot\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}{x}\]
\[a\cos\theta = \sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}\]
\[I = a\ln\left|\dfrac{a-\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}{x}\right| + \sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}} + c\]
Why: from \(\sin\theta = \frac{x}{a}\): hypotenuse \(a\), opposite \(x\), adjacent \(\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}\).

Check
The derivative of \(a\ln|a - \sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}| - a\ln|x| + \sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}\) is
\[\dfrac{ax}{\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}\,(a - \sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}})}\]
\[- \dfrac{a}{x} - \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}\]
which simplifies to \(\frac{\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}{x}\) (multiply the first fraction by \(\frac{a+\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}{a+\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}\) to get \(\frac{a(a+\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}})}{x\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}\)); checked also with sympy.
